Should include imports, class definition, @Test methods. Use JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test, org.junit.Assert). Also test for UnsupportedOperationException on mutator methods. Need to test applyPattern, toPattern, handling of custom format factories, parsing, quoted strings, edge cases like null pattern? Constructor throws IllegalArgumentException for bad pattern. Provide a dummy FormatFactory implementation for custom formats.

We need to list public methods: constructors are public. Methods: toPattern(), applyPattern(String), setFormat, setFormatByArgumentIndex, setFormats, setFormatsByArgumentIndex. Also inherited methods from MessageFormat but not overridden; but we only need those defined here.

Edge cases: pattern with custom format name that is not in registry (should treat as normal). pattern with custom format that returns a Format. pattern with escaped quotes. pattern with missing closing brace -> IllegalArgumentException. pattern with invalid argument index (non-digit) -> IllegalArgumentException. Test containsElements private not needed.

We'll need a simple FormatFactory interface (from org.apache.commons.lang.text.FormatFactory). Not in provided code but we can stub. Actually Apache commons has FormatFactory with method getFormat(String name, String args, Locale locale). We'll create a dummy inner class implementing it.

Test cases:

- testBasicPattern: new ExtendedMessageFormat("Hello {0}"); assertEquals("Hello {0}", emf.toPattern());

- testApplyPatternWithCustomFormat: registry with factory for "upper" that returns a Format that uppercases strings. pattern "Msg {0,upper}". Expect toPattern returns same pattern. Also format an object: emf.format(new Object[]{"test"}) returns "Msg TEST". Ensure custom format applied.

- testUnsupportedSetFormat: expect UnsupportedOperationException.

- testInvalidPatternMissingBrace: new ExtendedMessageFormat("{0"); expect IllegalArgumentException.

- testInvalidArgumentIndex: pattern "{x}" should throw IllegalArgumentException.

- testEscapedQuote: pattern "He''llo {0}" -> toPattern should preserve escaped quote? Actually MessageFormat treats '' as a single quote. We'll test formatting.

- testQuotedString: pattern "'{'0'}'" which should output {0} literal. Use format.

- testCustomFormatWithArgs: factory that takes args, e.g., "repeat,3" returns format that repeats string 3 times. Pattern "{0,repeat,3}"? format description includes comma; but parsing logic splits at first comma. We'll test.

Simplify: implement a RepeatFormat extends Format.
